logicalBugs.description: In Gitea, after Cancel in an issue (a tracked work item) or pull request (a proposed code change) title editor, reopening it reuses the discarded title or target-branch selection. On a pull request, saving a later title edit can therefore also apply the previously cancelled target-branch change.
logicalBugs.rootCause: initRepoIssueTitleEdit uses one Cancel handler for the title and pull-target controls. It only hides the shared editor; it never resets the title value or #pull-target-branch data-branch to the saved values. Reopening/submitting reuses those stale controls.
reproductionPaths: In Gitea, edit an issue title, type a replacement and click Cancel. The saved heading returns, but reopening Edit shows the discarded replacement in the textbox instead of resetting the editor to the saved title.

logicalBugs.description: In a Gitea issue’s Branch/Tag sidebar picker, choosing a tag does not save the reference, and Clear current reference also does nothing when used from the Tags tab. The same controls work from the Branches tab.
logicalBugs.rootCause: initBranchSelector queries only the first .reference-list-menu (Branches) and binds its items. The separate Tags menu, including its Clear item, receives no update handler.
reproductionPaths: In Gitea, open an issue’s Branch/Tag sidebar picker, choose Tags and select an existing tag. The picker closes but the issue still has no saved reference, rather than displaying and retaining the selected tag.

In a Gitea issue’s Branch/Tag selector, set a branch reference and then use Clear current reference from the Tags tab. The menu closes but the branch remains saved, with no change event; the same Clear action works from the Branches tab.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea, on global or organization Issues and Pull Requests, selecting an Author or Assignee and then clicking Open, Closed or an ownership sidebar link drops that user filter. Results and counts broaden to records excluded by the previously selected author/assignee, including when the ownership link was already active.
logicalBugs.rootCause: The dashboard builds $queryLink without poster or assignee, then uses it for ownership and Open/Closed links. $queryLinkWithFilter contains those fields but is only used by the filter and sort controls. Global and organization dashboards share this template.
reproductionPaths: Gitea’s top-level Issues dashboard loses its selected assignee/author filter when Open or Closed is clicked, broadening the results to unrelated issues.
On a Gitea organization's Issues page, clicking Open or Closed while an Assignee (or Author) is selected drops that filter, so the counts widen and unassigned issues appear.

On Gitea’s global Issues page, after selecting an Assignee filter, clicking an ownership link such as Created by you drops the assignee, so issues assigned to other users appear and the counts change.

On a Gitea organization's Issues page, with an Assignee filter applied, clicking the already-selected 'In your repositories' sidebar entry removes the assignee from the URL, so unassigned issues reappear. The sort order is kept.

logicalBugs.description: Gitea’s Issues list displays a total for time logged against the filtered work items. When a text search matches no issues, the rows correctly show no results but the tracked-time total still includes excluded issues instead of becoming zero.
logicalBugs.rootCause: The list passes an empty IssueIDs slice for zero keyword matches. The aggregate delegates to IssuesOptions conditions, which add an issue.id restriction only when len(IssueIDs)>0, conflating no matches with no restriction.
reproductionPaths: Gitea’s Issues list displays a total for time logged against the filtered work items. When a text search matches no issues, the rows correctly show no results but the tracked-time total still includes excluded issues instead of becoming zero.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea, issue and milestone (a named group of work items) due dates that coincide with unset-date sentinel values, including January 1 of year 0001 or 1970, can save and remain visible in the editor but display as a dash or missing date in timeline/list views. The defect concerns an accepted date disappearing from presentation, rather than an editor rejecting it.
logicalBugs.rootCause: Issue deadline comments and milestone date templates pass date-only strings through DateUtils.ParseLegacy, which reconstructs midnight in the server UI timezone. The shared anyToTime/dateTimeFormat renderer treats either Go zero time (0001-01-01 midnight in a matching timezone) or Unix timestamp 0 (1970-01-01 midnight UTC) as a missing value and prints a dash. A saved end-of-day deadline may be nonzero while this reparsed display value hits a zero sentinel; each reproduction path retains its specific date/timezone trigger.
reproductionPaths: In Gitea, set an issue due date to the accepted date January 1 of year 0001. Its sidebar shows the saved date, but the activity timeline substitutes a dash, including when a later edit describes the previous value.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea, an issue’s Participants sidebar lists the people involved in that work item. With exactly one participant, its heading reads “1 Participants,” using plural wording instead of “1 Participant.”
logicalBugs.rootCause: The English translation has a single %d Participants string and the sidebar passes the count to it without singular selection.
reproductionPaths: In Gitea, an issue’s Participants sidebar lists the people involved in that work item. With exactly one participant, its heading reads “1 Participants,” using plural wording instead of “1 Participant.”

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea, close with Comment is intended to post a comment and close an issue (a tracked work item) in one action. If an open dependency prevents closing, the comment is still saved but is not shown and its text remains in the editor. Retrying saves the same text again, and reloading reveals duplicate comments even though each attempt appeared only to fail.
logicalBugs.rootCause: CreateComment persists the comment before its deferred status change. If dependency validation rejects closure, the defer returns a JSON error before the redirect that would show the new comment and reset the editor. Retrying repeats comment creation.
reproductionPaths: In Gitea, close with Comment is intended to post a comment and close an issue in one action. If an open dependency prevents closing, the comment is still saved but is not shown and its text remains in the editor. Retrying saves the same text again, and reloading reveals duplicate comments even though each attempt appeared only to fail.

logicalBugs.description: Gitea’s issue (a tracked work item) comment composer supports uploading attachments before posting. After an image finishes uploading, an otherwise empty composer still keeps Comment disabled, preventing an attachment-only comment; adding text enables the button. This concerns posting the attachment without closing or reopening the issue.
logicalBugs.rootCause: syncUiState disables Comment whenever editor text is empty, ignoring completed uploaded files, although the server explicitly accepts empty content with attachments.
reproductionPaths: Gitea’s issue comment composer supports uploading attachments before posting. After an image finishes uploading, an otherwise empty composer still keeps Comment disabled, preventing an attachment-only comment; adding text enables the button. This concerns posting the attachment without closing or reopening the issue.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea, on an unfiltered Issues list, the Open count is expected to show open work items. Clicking that count instead selects all states and includes a closed issue, so the destination does not match the status named by the control.
logicalBugs.rootCause: The shared openclose template deliberately selects $allStatesLink when the clicked state equals .State. The Open label does not indicate that its destination becomes state=all.
reproductionPaths: In Gitea, on an unfiltered Issues list, the Open count is expected to show open work items. Clicking that count instead selects all states and includes a closed issue, so the destination does not match the status named by the control.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea, deleting an issue (a tracked work item) or pull request (a proposed code change) discussion comment removes its timeline card immediately, but the issue comment total or pull request Conversation badge keeps the previous count. Reload is needed for the header count to agree with the remaining comments.
logicalBugs.rootCause: The delete handler removes the timeline DOM node and updates review counters, but never changes the issue header count, leaving the original server-rendered value until navigation.
reproductionPaths: In Gitea, delete the only comment from an issue’s discussion. Its timeline card disappears immediately, but the header still reports one comment until reload instead of reflecting the empty discussion.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea, global/organization dashboards can list and count issues (tracked work items) or pull requests (proposed code changes) from a repository whose corresponding unit is disabled, and organization/team issue dashboards can include issues for a Code-only team without Issues access. The title remains actionable but opens 404 even though the repository itself may be readable.
logicalBugs.rootCause: SearchRepositoryCondition admits owned organization repositories and checks actor access with unit.TypeInvalid. The Issues UnitType does not constrain those repositories; dashboard search then loads their issues without per-issue unit authorization. Both disabled trackers and teams with Issues No Access pass this same repository selection.
reproductionPaths: In Gitea, disabling a repository issue tracker leaves its open issue in organization and global dashboard results/counts, with an actionable title leading to 404.

In Gitea, a team member whose team has Code Read but Issues No Access on a private organization repository can't open that repository's issues, but the organization (and team) Issues dashboards still list them with title, repository and number, author and Open count.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea, combining a matching keyword with Assigned to you or an Assignee filter can hide correctly assigned issues (tracked work items) and pull requests (proposed code changes) on repository, global and organization lists. Explicit user and Assigned to anybody filters are affected; either the keyword alone or the assignment-filtered list without a keyword can still find the same record.
logicalBugs.rootCause: Indexer conversion copies Issue.AssigneeID, a nonpersisted legacy field, instead of Issue.Assignees. Specific, self and any-assignee filters therefore query incorrect indexed data. Non-keyword database filtering uses issue_assignees and succeeds.
reproductionPaths: On Gitea’s global Issues dashboard, use a matching title search under Assigned to you for an issue assigned to the signed-in user. The issue disappears, although the same matching search under Created by you can list it.
In a Gitea repository's issue list, searching a fresh issue's title lists it, but adding the Assignee filter for its visible assignee shows No results.

On a Gitea organization's Issues page, 'Assigned to you' with a search query returns no results even though an issue assigned to the signed-in user matches it; the same query under 'In your repositories' lists the issue.

On a Gitea organization’s Issues dashboard, search for a word matching an issue assigned to a known user, then choose that user in Assignee. The matching issue disappears instead of remaining in the combined search and assignment results, although either restriction alone can find it.

On a Gitea repository's Issues list, choosing Type → Assigned to you while a text search is active shows No results, even though an issue assigned to you matches the search. The search index doesn't store current assignees.

On a Gitea repository’s Issues list, combine a matching keyword with Assignee > Assigned to anybody. Assigned issues that appear under either filter alone disappear, and both status counts become zero, despite their saved assignments remaining visible.
On Gitea’s global Issues page, with a text search active, choosing a user in the Assignee filter shows No results even though an issue assigned to that user matches the search.

logicalBugs.description: Gitea’s issue-list bulk Close action silently skips issues (tracked work items) with open dependencies. It deselects the issue and leaves it Open without explaining why, while the individual Close Issue action reports the blocking dependency.
logicalBugs.rootCause: The server returns HTTP 412 for blocked closure. updateIssuesMeta awaits POST without checking response.ok, and the caller reloads as though the change succeeded, losing selection and error details.
reproductionPaths: Gitea’s issue-list bulk Close action silently skips issues with open dependencies. It deselects the issue and leaves it Open without explaining why, while the individual Close Issue action reports the blocking dependency.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea, dependency validation prevents direct two-issue cycles but accepts transitive cycles. Three open issues (tracked work items) can each become blocked by another issue in the cycle, leaving all unable to close until a dependency is removed.
logicalBugs.rootCause: CreateIssueDependency checks issueDepExists(dep.ID, issue.ID) rather than transitive reachability. Three or more edges can form a cycle that blocks every close operation.
reproductionPaths: In Gitea, dependency validation prevents direct two-issue cycles but accepts transitive cycles. Three open issues can each become blocked by another issue in the cycle, leaving all unable to close until a dependency is removed.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea, an issue (a tracked work item) can be prevented from closing until its blocking dependencies are closed. Attempting to close such an issue while its timer is running correctly leaves the issue open, but stops the timer without updating the Time Tracker controls. Stop timer and Discard timer remain visible until reload, suggesting the timer is still running.
logicalBugs.rootCause: CloseIssue explicitly calls FinishIssueStopwatchIfPossible after receiving ErrDependenciesLeft, while the rejected response does not reload the sidebar. However, persistence needs transaction-level confirmation: models/issues.CloseIssue opens a nested TxContext whose uncommitted halfCommitter.Close rolls back/closes the shared session before the outer error branch attempts to finish the timer. The observed logged/stopped timer may depend on subsequent xorm session behavior; merely identifying the finish call does not prove which writes commit. The two paths retain their distinct persisted-state and stale-controls expectations. This is a source-informed hypothesis; the exact mechanism has not been confirmed in execution.
reproductionPaths: In Gitea, an issue can be prevented from closing until its blocking dependencies are closed. Attempting to close such an issue while its timer is running correctly leaves the issue open, but stops the timer without updating the Time Tracker controls. Stop timer and Discard timer remain visible until reload, suggesting the timer is still running.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea, Quote Reply on an issue (a tracked work item) or pull request (a proposed code change) inserts nonempty quoted text into the comment composer, but Comment stays disabled and switching to Preview/Write does not enable it. Typing an ordinary character can make the same composer submittable.
logicalBugs.rootCause: tryOnQuoteReply uses ComboMarkdownEditor.value(v). The textarea setter changes value without dispatching EventEditorContentChanged, while comment button state listens to that event and upload events. Typing finally resynchronizes it.
reproductionPaths: On a Gitea issue discussion, choose Quote Reply for a comment. The quotation appears in the composer, but Comment remains disabled and the adjacent action still says Close Issue; an ordinary space/backspace edit enables posting even when the final text is unchanged.

logicalBugs.description: In a Gitea issue’s Manually Add Time dialog, submitting a negative duration correctly leaves the dialog open and records no time. The error message exposes internal RangeError text instead of a readable explanation of the allowed duration; the defect is feedback, not accepting the negative time.
logicalBugs.rootCause: Hours is constrained with binding Range(0,1000). AddTimeManually returns the generic form error via GetErrMsg before reaching its readable duration validation, exposing the untranslated range binding feedback.
reproductionPaths: In a Gitea issue’s Manually Add Time dialog, submitting a negative duration correctly leaves the dialog open and records no time. The error message exposes internal RangeError text instead of a readable explanation of the allowed duration; the defect is feedback, not accepting the negative time.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea, after inline editing and saving an issue (a tracked work item) body or pull request (a proposed code change) description, newly rendered Markdown task-list checkboxes no longer respond or persist clicks. Reloading the page restores working checkboxes for that same saved text.
logicalBugs.rootCause: saveAndRefresh replaces renderContent.innerHTML but only attaches reference popups; it never calls initMarkupTasklist on the replacement markup. Page initialization attaches those handlers after reload.
reproductionPaths: In Gitea, after adding task-list items to an issue body with inline Edit, clicking a new unchecked box does nothing; after a reload the same click checks and saves it.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea, on global or organization Issues and Pull Requests, submitting a text search clears the selected Author or Assignee. The search results then include matching records by other authors or assigned to other users/nobody, even though the user intended to narrow the existing filtered list.
logicalBugs.rootCause: The shared dashboard search form submits only type, sort, state and search-combo fields. It has no poster or assignee hidden input, so submitting a keyword discards those filters on both global and organization dashboards.
reproductionPaths: In Gitea, submitting search on the top-level Issues dashboard drops the selected assignee filter and displays a matching unassigned issue that was excluded before the search.
On Gitea’s top-level Issues dashboard, submitting a text search clears the selected Author filter, so issues by other authors appear in the results.
On a Gitea organization's Issues page, submitting a text search while an Author is selected drops the Author filter, so issues by other authors that match the search appear.
On a Gitea organization's Issues page, submitting a text search while an Assignee is selected drops the Assignee filter, so unassigned issues that match the search appear.

logicalBugs.description: On Gitea’s global Issues or Pull Requests dashboard, choosing an explicit Author or Assignee does not give the filter control a visible active state distinct from no filter. The URL/results may be filtered correctly, but the closed controls do not reveal that restriction.
logicalBugs.rootCause: filter_item_user_fetch records the selected username only in a data attribute used inside the remote dropdown. The closed control always renders the same title and classes, regardless of selection.
reproductionPaths: On Gitea’s global Issues dashboard, choose a specific user in the Assignee filter. The closed filter control still looks like the unfiltered Assignee control, without the chosen name or an active indicator, even though the list is restricted to that user.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea, when issues (tracked work items) with different due dates are assigned to an existing milestone (a named group of work items) with no due date, Farthest due date sorts them by creation order instead of their issue dates. Without the milestone, or with Nearest due date, the issue-date order is correct.
logicalBugs.rootCause: The DESC CASE handles NULL milestone deadlines but not 0. The next branch selects milestone.deadline_unix=0 over a positive issue deadline; the ASC implementation explicitly handles zero and works.
reproductionPaths: In Gitea, when issues with different due dates are assigned to an existing milestone with no due date, Farthest due date sorts them by creation order instead of their issue dates. Without the milestone, or with Nearest due date, the issue-date order is correct.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea, saving a time estimate (or manual time) succeeds on the server, but the page then reloads to show it. When any other form on the issue (a tracked work item) page counts as unsaved, the browser asks whether to leave the page; choosing to stay leaves the dialog spinning forever and every later Save does nothing. Cancelling a time-tracker dialog is enough to make its form count as unsaved, so the warning can appear with no real unsaved work.
logicalBugs.rootCause: On HTTP 200 fetchActionDoRequest ignores dirty state only for the submitted form, calls reload/redirect, then returns before removing is-loading. A different dirty form can cancel navigation; the successful dialog remains locked because later submits return while is-loading is set.
reproductionPaths: In Gitea, saving a time estimate (or manual time) succeeds on the server, but the page then reloads to show it. When any other form on the issue page counts as unsaved, the browser asks whether to leave the page; choosing to stay leaves the dialog spinning forever and every later Save does nothing. Cancelling a time-tracker dialog is enough to make its form count as unsaved, so the warning can appear with no real unsaved work.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea, deleting an issue never removes it from the issue search index, so keyword searches on the global Issues dashboard keep counting the deleted issue in the Open/Closed and sidebar totals and reserve page slots for it, while the list itself shows only the issues (tracked work items) that still exist.
logicalBugs.rootCause: DeleteIssue emits a notification, but indexerNotifier inherits the no-op DeleteIssue from NullNotifier rather than deleting the indexed document. Indexed counts and slots outlive the database issue; row loading drops the deleted row.
reproductionPaths: In Gitea, deleting an issue never removes it from the issue search index, so keyword searches on the global Issues dashboard keep counting the deleted issue in the Open/Closed and sidebar totals and reserve page slots for it, while the list itself shows only the issues that still exist.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea, issue and pull request (a proposed code change) form actions can expose a raw JSON-parsing SyntaxError labelled Network error when the server rejects an unavailable or unauthorized action. Confirmed triggers include stale deleted/locked/archived comment or issue (a tracked work item) forms, deleted milestone (a named group of work items)/time-entry targets and rejected review actions; the UI does not explain the actual refusal.
logicalBugs.rootCause: fetchActionDoRequest unconditionally calls resp.json() for HTTP 4xx and labels parsing exceptions Network error. Plain-text missing-issue/permission responses therefore expose SyntaxError rather than the rejection reason. Deleted comment inline edits use a separate parser and are kept separate.
reproductionPaths: In Gitea, if another user locks an issue while a non-collaborator has a comment draft open, clicking Comment shows a 'Network error SyntaxError … is not valid JSON' toast instead of saying the conversation is locked.

In Gitea, submitting a comment from an issue tab left open before deletion shows an internal JSON parsing exception mislabeled as a network error rather than explaining that the issue no longer exists.

In Gitea, submitting Manually Add Time from an issue tab opened before the issue was deleted leaves the dialog open and shows a technical JSON parsing error instead of explaining that the issue no longer exists.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea’s repository Settings, the External Issue Tracker's Regular Expression Pattern accepts a malformed pattern such as '[' and shows 'The repository settings have been updated.' Issue references then stop linking.
logicalBugs.rootCause: handleSettingsPostAdvanced validates tracker URLs but assigns ExternalTrackerRegexpPattern directly to the unit configuration without compiling it, allowing invalid expressions to persist and disable reference matching.
reproductionPaths: In Gitea’s repository Settings, the External Issue Tracker's Regular Expression Pattern accepts a malformed pattern such as '[' and shows 'The repository settings have been updated.' Issue references then stop linking.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea, editing an issue's due date to a date with a five-digit year (for example 10000-01-01, or a typo like 20270-01-15) saves without an error but deletes the existing due date, and the timeline records it as removed.
logicalBugs.rootCause: UpdateIssueDeadline ignores the error returned by ParseDeadlineDateToEndOfDay. A five-digit year fails the Go date layout and returns zero; UpdateIssueDeadline interprets zero as delete.
reproductionPaths: In Gitea, editing an issue's due date to a date with a five-digit year (for example 10000-01-01, or a typo like 20270-01-15) saves without an error but deletes the existing due date, and the timeline records it as removed.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea, on a locked issue (a tracked work item) or pull request (a proposed code change), a user without write access has no comment box, but the ⋯ menu on the description and comments still offers Quote Reply. Clicking it does nothing visible except a JavaScript error.
logicalBugs.rootCause: The quote menu remains rendered on locked discussions for readers who cannot comment. tryOnQuoteReply assumes #comment-form has a ComboMarkdownEditor and dereferences editor.value() without a missing-editor guard.
reproductionPaths: In Gitea, on a locked issue or pull request, a user without write access has no comment box, but the ⋯ menu on the description and comments still offers Quote Reply. Clicking it does nothing visible except a JavaScript error.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea, for an attachment whose file name contains an unmatched square bracket (such as 'UP ] image.png' or 'y [ z.png'), the upload's Copy link inserts the name into the Markdown label without escaping, so the pasted text renders as literal Markdown instead of an image or link. Ordinary names and balanced brackets work.
logicalBugs.rootCause: dropzone constructs link/image Markdown by interpolating file.name directly between brackets. Unmatched brackets break the generated syntax; HTML escaping in other media branches does not protect these Markdown labels.
reproductionPaths: In Gitea, for an attachment whose file name contains an unmatched square bracket (such as 'UP ] image.png' or 'y [ z.png'), the upload's Copy link inserts the name into the Markdown label without escaping, so the pasted text renders as literal Markdown instead of an image or link. Ordinary names and balanced brackets work.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea, when an @mention is added to an issue (a tracked work item) by editing an existing comment or the issue description, the mentioned user's issue list filter 'Mentioning you' doesn't include that issue. A mention in a newly posted comment is included.
logicalBugs.rootCause: CreateIssueComment calls FindAndUpdateIssueMentions, but UpdateComment and ChangeContent do not perform the corresponding mention membership update. Mentioning you filters rely on those rows, so edited-in mentions are absent.
reproductionPaths: In Gitea, when an @mention is added to an issue by editing an existing comment or the issue description, the mentioned user's issue list filter 'Mentioning you' doesn't include that issue. A mention in a newly posted comment is included.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea’s repository Settings, if an invalid value is typed into the External Issue Tracker URL and the tracker is switched back to Built-In, the hidden, inactive URL field still fails browser validation. Update Settings then does nothing, so valid changes such as Time Tracking are never saved, with no visible message.
logicalBugs.rootCause: The advanced settings form hides the external tracker controls when Built-In is selected without disabling their URL input. Native URL validity checks still reject that hidden input and prevent the entire form submit.
reproductionPaths: In Gitea’s repository Settings, if an invalid value is typed into the External Issue Tracker URL and the tracker is switched back to Built-In, the hidden, inactive URL field still fails browser validation. Update Settings then does nothing, so valid changes such as Time Tracking are never saved, with no visible message.

logicalBugs.description: On Gitea’s Issues lists, Oldest order puts issues (tracked work items) created in the same second lowest number first, but adding a text search keyword flips them so the higher-numbered issue comes first. Keyword searches go through the search index, which breaks creation-time ties by id descending for every sort, while the unsearched list breaks Oldest ties by id ascending.
logicalBugs.rootCause: Bleve search always appends -_id to its sort. For oldest, equal created times therefore sort newest ID first, unlike the database ascending creation/id ordering.
reproductionPaths: On Gitea’s Issues lists, Oldest order puts issues created in the same second lowest number first, but adding a text search keyword flips them so the higher-numbered issue comes first. Keyword searches go through the search index, which breaks creation-time ties by id descending for every sort, while the unsearched list breaks Oldest ties by id ascending.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea, issues, Pull Requests and milestone (a named group of work items) issue (a tracked work item) lists advertise Alt+Enter to exclude a label, but using that keyboard shortcut includes the label instead. Alt+click on the same label correctly applies the exclusion.
logicalBugs.rootCause: The exclusion listener is attached to the dropdown keydown, but the Fomantic keyboard path selects/activates the anchor on Enter. Its normal include navigation runs instead of the intended exclusion navigation, whereas the direct Alt+click handler sees the modifier.
reproductionPaths: Gitea’s issue list's Label filter says 'Use alt + click/enter to exclude labels'. Alt+click excludes the label, but highlighting a label with the keyboard and pressing Alt+Enter includes it, so issues without that label disappear from the list.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea, after editing an issue's description (or a comment) and clicking Cancel, the saved text stays rendered, but reopening Edit without refreshing shows the cancelled draft instead of the saved text. Clicking Update from there saves the discarded draft.
logicalBugs.rootCause: cancelAndReset hides the editor and reloads attachments without resetting its text. Reopening populates rawContent only if the cached editor value is empty, so a nonempty discarded draft is reused.
reproductionPaths: In Gitea, after editing an issue's description (or a comment) and clicking Cancel, the saved text stays rendered, but reopening Edit without refreshing shows the cancelled draft instead of the saved text. Clicking Update from there saves the discarded draft.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea, an issue (a tracked work item) timer control left open in one tab performs the opposite action after the timer changes in another tab. A stale Stop starts a new timer, while a stale Start stops the running timer and logs time, rather than preserving the Start/Stop intent shown to the user.
logicalBugs.rootCause: IssueStopwatch forwards both buttons to CreateOrStopIssueStopwatch without an intended target state. Requests from stale tabs toggle the current server state in the opposite direction from the button label.
reproductionPaths: In Gitea, with an issue open in two tabs, stop its running timer in one tab and then click the stale Stop timer button in the other. A new timer starts instead of keeping the timer stopped as that button requests.

In Gitea, with an issue open in two tabs, start its timer in one tab and then click the stale Start timer button in the other. The running timer stops and logs time instead of keeping it running as the visible Start action requests.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea, after saving the first inline edit of an issue (a tracked work item) comment or description, the new text appears but the '• edited' indicator and its revision-history menu don't appear until the page is reloaded, even though the server already recorded the revision.
logicalBugs.rootCause: saveAndRefresh replaces the rendered body, raw content, attachments and content-version attribute, but never refreshes the comment header containing the edited/history control. The server records the revision and reload renders it.
reproductionPaths: In Gitea, after saving the first inline edit of an issue comment or description, the new text appears but the '• edited' indicator and its revision-history menu don't appear until the page is reloaded, even though the server already recorded the revision.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea, set or change an issue (a tracked work item) or pull request’s due date in its sidebar, then search for matching text and sort by Nearest or Farthest due date. Global searches, and the repository issue-search path, can display the new dates but order results using earlier dates or as if no date were set. Posting an ordinary comment on the affected work item makes the search order catch up.
logicalBugs.rootCause: UpdateIssueDeadline updates the database and timeline only; indexerNotifier has no due-date change hook. Keyword searches sort the indexed DeadlineUnix from the last indexing job until another supported notification reindexes the issue.
reproductionPaths: On Gitea’s global Issues dashboard, search for a shared keyword and sort issues by due date after changing an existing due date in the sidebar. The rows display the changed date, but the ordering still follows the previous date until another action such as an ordinary comment refreshes it.

In Gitea, create issues without due dates, add their dates later in the sidebar, then search their shared keyword on the global Issues dashboard and sort by due date. The list orders them as though their new dates were absent instead of using the dates displayed on the rows.

In a Gitea repository’s Issues list, give newly created issues due dates in the sidebar, then search their shared keyword and choose Farthest due date. A nearer-due issue can appear before a farther-due issue even though both saved dates are displayed correctly.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea, if an attachment is added to a comment and saved in one tab, then a comment editor opened earlier in another tab is saved (for example after removing an original attachment, or with only a text change), the newer attachment is deleted from the comment and from storage without any warning. Text-only conflicts are detected, but attachment-only changes don't update the comment's version.
logicalBugs.rootCause: UpdateCommentContent increments the comment content version only when text differs. Attachment updates run separately without changing that version, allowing a stale editor to pass the version check and replace/delete newer attachments.
reproductionPaths: In Gitea, if an attachment is added to a comment and saved in one tab, then a comment editor opened earlier in another tab is saved (for example after removing an original attachment, or with only a text change), the newer attachment is deleted from the comment and from storage without any warning. Text-only conflicts are detected, but attachment-only changes don't update the comment's version.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea, turning off a repository’s Issues or Pull Requests unit and later re-enabling it loses that unit’s saved options. Issue tracker restrictions or pull-request merge/deletion choices return to defaults rather than the settings used before the unit was disabled.
logicalBugs.rootCause: handleSettingsPostAdvanced removes disabled RepoUnit records instead of retaining their configuration. When a unit is re-enabled, newRepoUnit builds a fresh record from the defaults rendered in settings. The shared repository-unit lifecycle therefore loses both Issues and Pull Requests configuration.
reproductionPaths: In Gitea, turn a repository’s issue tracker off, save, then enable it again. Previously saved options such as disabling time tracking or dependencies return to checked defaults instead of being restored; this concerns re-enabling the same feature, not replacing an external integration with a different one.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea, when an issue (a tracked work item) in a repository is linked as depending on (or blocking) an issue in a private repository, the issue's timeline shows the private repository's name and the private issue's title to every reader, including users with no access to the private repository. The sidebar on the same page correctly hides the dependency, and the API timeline also returns the private issue.
logicalBugs.rootCause: Comment.LoadDepIssueDetails loads the linked issue by ID with no actor permission filtering. The timeline renders its repository/title and conversion can expose it through the API, while the sidebar separately restricts unreadable dependencies.
reproductionPaths: In Gitea, when an issue in a repository is linked as depending on (or blocking) an issue in a private repository, the issue's timeline shows the private repository's name and the private issue's title to every reader, including users with no access to the private repository. The sidebar on the same page correctly hides the dependency, and the API timeline also returns the private issue.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea, if time tracking is disabled in a repository's settings while a user's timer is running on one of its issues (tracked work items), the header still shows the active timer, but Stop and Discard fail with "Network error SyntaxError: … 'Not found.' is not valid JSON", and the timer can never be stopped.
logicalBugs.rootCause: IssueStopwatch and CancelStopwatch both require CanUseTimetracker before changing state. That permission rejects a disabled unit even for an already-running timer; disabling the repository setting does not clean up those timers.
reproductionPaths: In Gitea, if time tracking is disabled in a repository's settings while a user's timer is running on one of its issues, the header still shows the active timer, but Stop and Discard fail with "Network error SyntaxError: … 'Not found.' is not valid JSON", and the timer can never be stopped.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea, if a time log on an issue (a tracked work item) is deleted in one tab, clicking delete on the same log in another tab that hasn't been reloaded shows a red "server error: 500" instead of saying the entry no longer exists.
logicalBugs.rootCause: GetTrackedTimeByID returns soft-deleted records. DeleteTime then receives db.ErrNotExist from deleteTime, but its post-delete error branch always returns ServerError rather than a missing/already-deleted response.
reproductionPaths: In Gitea, if a time log on an issue is deleted in one tab, clicking delete on the same log in another tab that hasn't been reloaded shows a red "server error: 500" instead of saying the entry no longer exists.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea, when an issue (a tracked work item) body (or comment) already embeds one of its attached images, saving an inline edit adds a second thumbnail of that image below the attachment list until the page is reloaded.
logicalBugs.rootCause: saveAndRefresh inserts the attachment template returned by the server directly after replacing markup. The full-page image/attachment deduplication initialization is not rerun, so an embedded attachment gets an extra thumbnail until reload.
reproductionPaths: In Gitea, when an issue body (or comment) already embeds one of its attached images, saving an inline edit adds a second thumbnail of that image below the attachment list until the page is reloaded.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea, in an existing issue’s inline title editor, clear the title and click Save. The editor closes and restores the old title without saying that an empty title was rejected, so the attempted change appears to have been ignored rather than explained.
logicalBugs.rootCause: The submit handler skips POST when the trimmed title is empty but still ignores dirty state and reloads. It never returns validation feedback for the skipped save.
reproductionPaths: In Gitea, in an existing issue’s inline title editor, clear the title and click Save. The editor closes and restores the old title without saying that an empty title was rejected, so the attempted change appears to have been ignored rather than explained.

logicalBugs.description: On Gitea’s global Issues dashboard, a label filter reached through a label badge or organization label usage link is not preserved through subsequent sidebar/ownership navigation. The destination broadens the list instead of retaining the selected label.
logicalBugs.rootCause: buildIssueOverview reads the active labels query into opts.LabelIDs for database/search filtering but never assigns selectedLabels to ctx.Data["SelectLabels"]. The shared dashboard template builds its state and ownership links with .SelectLabels, so those links omit the active labels filter. This affects global and organization issue/PR dashboards.
reproductionPaths: On Gitea’s global Issues page, after filtering by a label (for example by clicking a label badge), clicking an ownership link such as Created by you drops the label filter, so issues without that label appear.

logicalBugs.description: On a Gitea repository's Issues list, combining a Project filter with a keyword search shows No results (or silently leaves out issues (tracked work items)) for issues added to the project after they were created, even though each filter alone lists them. A keyword search filters by the project stored in the search index, and adding or removing an issue's project (from the sidebar or the bulk Projects action) never updates the index, so it still has the old project until something else, such as a comment or label change, reindexes the issue. Removing a project has the reverse effect with the No project filter.
logicalBugs.rootCause: Project membership updates do not emit an issue-index refresh. Keyword search filters the ProjectID snapshot created by index conversion, while database-only filters use current membership; another indexing notification repairs it.
reproductionPaths: On a Gitea repository's Issues list, combining a Project filter with a keyword search shows No results (or silently leaves out issues) for issues added to the project after they were created, even though each filter alone lists them. A keyword search filters by the project stored in the search index, and adding or removing an issue's project (from the sidebar or the bulk Projects action) never updates the index, so it still has the old project until something else, such as a comment or label change, reindexes the issue. Removing a project has the reverse effect with the No project filter.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea, after choosing Type > Assigned to you, switching back to All issues (tracked work items) or to another ownership type can retain the old implicit assignee restriction. Repository/milestone (a named group of work items) issue lists and organization pull request (a proposed code change) lists then omit otherwise matching records despite showing the new Type selection.
logicalBugs.rootCause: The issue handler exports the effective self assignee after Type=assigned; shared filter_list copies that AssigneeID into subsequent Type links. Created by you therefore retains an unintended assignment restriction.
reproductionPaths: On a Gitea repository's Issues list, choosing Type > Assigned to you and then Type > All issues still shows only issues assigned to you (with a search, the list stays empty), instead of returning to all matching issues.

logicalBugs.description: On a Gitea issue (a tracked work item) that depends on an issue the user can't read, the sidebar shows a lock and says the user can still remove the dependency. Confirming Remove opens a completely blank page, and the dependency is not removed.
logicalBugs.rootCause: Locked Depends-on rows emit dependency-type blocking instead of blockedBy. RemoveDependency attempts to delete the reversed edge; ErrDependencyNotExists sets a flash error then returns without a redirect/body, producing a blank 200 page.
reproductionPaths: On a Gitea issue that depends on an issue the user can't read, the sidebar shows a lock and says the user can still remove the dependency. Confirming Remove opens a completely blank page, and the dependency is not removed.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea, if a comment is deleted (for example from another tab) while its inline editor is open, clicking Save shows a technical error banner, 'Failed to save the content: SyntaxError: Unexpected token 'N', "Not found." is not valid JSON', instead of explaining that the comment no longer exists. The editor closes and the old comment text is shown.
logicalBugs.rootCause: saveAndRefresh calls response.json() before checking HTTP status and only renders structured errorMessage for 400. A plain-text 404 from UpdateCommentContent for a deleted comment throws into the raw exception toast.
reproductionPaths: In Gitea, if a comment is deleted (for example from another tab) while its inline editor is open, clicking Save shows a technical error banner, 'Failed to save the content: SyntaxError: Unexpected token 'N', "Not found." is not valid JSON', instead of explaining that the comment no longer exists. The editor closes and the old comment text is shown.

logicalBugs.description: In a Gitea repository's Settings > Advanced Settings, submitting the external issue (a tracked work item) tracker with an invalid URL shows the error, but the form reloads with Built-In issue tracker selected, the URL Format empty and no number style chosen, discarding everything the user entered.
logicalBugs.rootCause: handleSettingsPostAdvanced handles invalid tracker URLs/formats by flashing an error and redirecting to settings. That GET renders persisted unit settings instead of the submitted draft, resetting other entered values.
reproductionPaths: In a Gitea repository's Settings > Advanced Settings, submitting the external issue tracker with an invalid URL shows the error, but the form reloads with Built-In issue tracker selected, the URL Format empty and no number style chosen, discarding everything the user entered.
